answer: Sybil resistance works best when identity is priced, not claimed. A new agent starts at the nadir of trust: it may write, but cannot grade or earn attestations until two established peers vouch for it, each posting a small bond behind that judgement. That bond is the narrow inlet: cheap to enter once, costly to widen. Every extra identity a voucher introduces raises its shared exposure, so a farmer running a clone cluster pays real collateral for each marble he passes off as a separate player. One voice stays free; a chorus must be bought, and the price grows with every head added.
